items.title: Somali forces report heavy fighting near Burhakaba as airstrike claims denied
items.description: Multiple sources reported fierce clashes in the area, with initial accounts indicating significant losses among federal government forces. Separate reports from Leego said several senior military commanders were missing. The number of casualties and the status of the missing commanders remained unclear. Al-Shabab also released photographs purporting to show Somali military vehicles burned during the fighting. The images could not be independently verified. However, the Somali federal government rejected reports that Turkish F-16 fighter jets or armed drones struck Somali National Army position
items.titleIt: Somali forces report heavy fighting near Burhakaba as airstrike claims denied

items.title: Somalia braces for El Niño floods as millions face risk of hunger
items.description: In Bayahaaw village, on the outskirts of Jowhar in central Somalia, farmers face a difficult choice: plant crops and risk losing them to floodwaters or leave their fields bare and face potential hunger in the coming year. Nuh Adan, a farmer and community leader in Bayahaaw, said flooding caused by breached riverbanks could devastate local agriculture for months. "If the river breaks and the floods hit us, the effects will last until the next rainy season in March," Adan said. items.title: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
items.description: The boat went down during the night of Oct. 8-9 near Guehere, north of the port town of Obock. The death toll rose from 109 after 30 more bodies were recovered, the International Organization for Migration said. About 82 people survived, while search and recovery operations continued. The shipwreck is among the deadliest recorded on the Eastern Route, a migration corridor used by people traveling from the Horn of Africa toward Yemen and other destinations in the Arabian Peninsula. items.titleIt: Death toll rises to 139 after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
